findings_contract: Gas forwarded: GAS then CALL at 1535/1536 and 3210/3211, so the asked gas is all gas left and the 63/64 rule decides (msg.gas = messageCallGas(...).subCall, exact in ok_reclaim). Value 0, so no stipend.

Checked by the bytes: msg.value == 0; CALLER == owner (slot 5 bits 8..167); EXTCODESIZE(token) != 0 before EACH call; success flag of each call (failure: RETURNDATACOPY of the whole return data to memory 0 and REVERT with it, proved byte exact); RETURNDATASIZE >= 32 after each call; first word of the second return != 0. The first returned word (the balance) is not checked, it is passed on as the amount.

Message 1: 36 bytes at memory 128: selector 0x70a08231, then address(this). Output range 128..160 (over the start of the input). Message 2: 68 bytes at memory 128: selector 0xa9059cbb, owner, balance; output 128..160.
The balance is read from memory 128 after the call; it is the first 32 returned bytes because RETURNDATASIZE >= 32 was checked first.

OWNER RE-READ: the owner in message 2 is SLOAD(5) of the state the first child left (rcOwner message child1.state), not the owner checked at the start. A callee that changed the owner of WBTC during balanceOf changes who is paid.

WBTC's own opcodes write no storage and emit no log in this function: the frame handed to each child differs from the state before only by records of reads (ReadsAs), logs equal (rcCallerSub_quiet); end state = child2.state.

Self call: token = WBTC passes the EXTCODESIZE test; WBTC then runs its own balanceOf and transfer as nested calls with msg.sender = WBTC. All theorems hold for it (no msg.currentTarget != L assumption); sane_of_sentVia proves the nested message runs CODE.
A token that is an EIP-7702 delegation is covered: SentVia says the message runs the code the state holds for the address the call resolves to.
Only the first argument word is read and its high 96 bits are masked; the call data size is not required to be 36.

finishMinting(): owner only, returns false (word 0), writes nothing, no log. No function sets mintingFinished: under Sep + AllowFixed no SINGLE call (a reclaimToken frame aside) changes that byte (Roles.mintingFinished_fixed). This is a per-call fact; there is no theorem over a sequence of calls or across a reclaimToken frame, so 'minting can never be finished' is the reading of the bytes, not a proved statement
renounceOwnership(): fails on every path (the owner path returns a reason string); ownership can not be renounced
transferOwnership(newOwner): owner only, only writes pendingOwner (low 160 bits of slot 6), owner unchanged, NO event, no zero-address check (0 and the owner itself accepted)
claimOwnership(): pending owner only; owner := pendingOwner, pendingOwner := 0, emits OwnershipTransferred(old, new); the log comes before the SSTOREs
mint(to, amount): owner only, needs mintingFinished = 0, NOT blocked by pause (witness mint_paused_runs), no check that to != 0 (can mint to address 0); logs Mint then Transfer(0, to, amount)
burn(value): owner only, burns the owner's OWN balance, NOT blocked by pause (witness burn_paused_runs); logs Burn then Transfer(owner, 0, value); returns nothing
pause blocks transfer, transferFrom, approve, increaseApproval, decreaseApproval; pause() needs not paused, unpause() needs paused; both owner only
transfer / transferFrom: to != 0 checked, to = the contract itself allowed; transferFrom lowers the allowance always (no infinite allowance) and emits no Approval
approve: no check of the old allowance, spender may be 0
decreaseApproval sets the allowance to 0 when subtracted >= old
no call-data size checks anywhere (solc 0.4.24): missing argument bytes read as zero
every plain function reverts on a non-zero call value
a token whose transfer returns 0 makes the whole call revert after both calls ran (SafeERC20 style check)

reclaimToken(WBTC) works as a direct self call: balanceOf then transfer with msg.sender = WBTC move WBTC's own balance to the owner; totalSupply_ and the sum of the two balances do not change. The inner transfer needs the token unpaused (whenNotPaused reads slot 5).
each CALL passes all gas but one 64th (63/64 rule); the witness needs about 60000 gas in the inner transfer
WBTC has no unbounded argument, so the frame theorems hold for every gas (LINK needed a gas cap).
Slot layout from the bytes: balances mapping slot 0, totalSupply_ slot 1, allowances mapping slot 2, slot 5 packs decimals / owner (bits 8..167) / mintingFinished / paused, pendingOwner slot 6.

global_keccak_hypotheses.result: Better than LINK on (b), and on (a) as far as the model allows. Both hypotheses are run-local now; the global SepAll and NoCollision remain only in corollaries with the hypothesis in the name. Non-reentrant theorems use only Sep (callKeys message); reclaimToken's own theorems use no keccak hypothesis.
global_keccak_hypotheses.a_NoCollision: Cannot be avoided in the model. Checked on the box's EthLib (commit 62dbd687): one code table keyed by hash, State.setCode does codeWrites.insert (keccak256 code) code (overwrite), getCode reads codeWrites first, then the parent's, then preState; the account only stores the hash. So a deposit of another byte string with the hash of CODE would change what L runs. Replaced by: no code deposited DURING THIS RUN is a different byte string with the hash of CODE (deposit events of Occurs).
global_keccak_hypotheses.b_SepAll: Replaced by Sep (callKeys m) only for messages m that enter L's code during the run (enter events of Occurs), and by the finite list form cleanW_of_sepList.
global_keccak_hypotheses.approach: Ideas (i) and (ii) of the brief together: an inductive trace relation (Sent, Occurs) that mirrors runFrame and processRunner, a Prop Clean over its events, and the induction redone. The key trick is the restricted runner `only` with runFrame_agree, which meets the universal KeepsOn hypothesis of the token theorem with knowledge of sent messages only.
global_keccak_hypotheses.satisfiable: Not shown satisfiable in closed form. cleanW_reclaim_tiny (real reclaimToken run against the tiny token) and cleanW_totalSupply show that the run-local condition follows from Sep (callKeys message) of the top message; cleanW_of_sepList reduces it to Sep of one caller-chosen finite list. Sep itself is never proved for any list. Only cleanFrameW_reclaim_tiny has no keccak hypothesis. For the token RE that calls back, CleanFrameW and CleanW follow from Sep RE_KEYS (five words): supply_reclaim_re_frame, process_reclaim_re.
global_keccak_hypotheses.missing: Clean for the self call and for failing reclaimToken runs (see not_covered). Sep (callKeys message) of the top message stays in the Clean forms even for reclaimToken, because Clean asks it uniformly of every message that enters WBTC; dropping it needs a per-selector condition.

reuse_notes.ports_back_to_LINK: Yes. Trace.lean is token independent (it imports only the token's copy of Reenter.lean and EthLib). For LINK: copy it, rename the namespace, prove FrameKeepsQ from LINK's supply_all with hsep := Q message (keeping LINK's GAS_CAP), then copy AnyLocal / SeqLocal with the names changed.
reuse_notes.CRO: 8,144 bytes, solc 0.4.24 optimized: generators run as for WBTC (same dispatcher, SafeMath, value check). 3 CALL sites, all the same compiler pattern as WBTC (EXTCODESIZE, GAS, CALL, bubble, RETURNDATASIZE check), so CallOut / CallBubble / callTail and the `segments` config apply as is: pc 3514 upgradeFrom (0x753e88e5) in upgrade(), AFTER 3 SSTOREs (balance, totalSupply, totalUpgraded) and before a LOG3; pc 5940 isUpgradeAgent (0x61d3d7a6) and pc 6295 originalSupply (0x4b2ba0dd) in setUpgradeAgent, after the SSTORE of upgradeAgent at pc 5851. New work: (1) the callee is a STORED address, not an argument; (2) upgrade() writes before the call, so the state handed to the child must already satisfy the invariant (burn of balance and totalSupply together: it does) and the theorem needs the write-then-call form of reclaim_good; (3) Trace / AnyLocal / SeqLocal copy over with names changed; a frame gas cap may be needed if CRO has unbounded arguments.
reuse_notes.LEO: 6,316 bytes, solc 0.5.1 optimized, MiniMe: much more than a rerun. CALL sites: pc 423 fallback proxyPayment (0xf48c3054) to the controller WITH VALUE (needs the value branch of the CALL rule, stipend and balance move: TokenKit Payee / Move / Stipend); pc 2454 onApprove (0xda682aeb) before the allowance SSTORE; pc 3193 STATICCALL balanceOfAt (0x4ee2cd7e) and pc 4461 STATICCALL totalSupplyAt (0x981b24d0) on parentToken (TokenKit StaticCall; a static child cannot write, so no reentrancy induction for these two, but their returned words enter the result); pc 3754 createCloneToken on the factory with dynamic strings and pc 3898 changeController (0x3cebb823) on the new clone; pc 4842 approveAndCall receiveApproval with dynamic bytes and output size 0 (like LINK's transferAndCall: gen_tac / tacsym); pc 5480 onTransfer (0x4a393149) to the controller. Also needed: checkpoint arrays (binary search loops, so a loop invariant and a different supply statement: the invariant is over the LAST checkpoint of each array), the NUMBER opcode, solc 0.5 dispatcher (CALLDATASIZE < 4, SHR-free but with the 0.5 revert shapes). CallOut covers value 0 CALLs only; the bubble tail of solc 0.5.1 should be checked against callTail (same shape expected). Trace.lean applies unchanged.
reuse_notes.general: For any token with outside calls: copy Reenter, CallIn, CallOut, CallBubble, Trace, Hold, AnyLocal, SeqLocal, use `segments` in the config, prove the <fn>_good theorem by hand from the segment theorems, then the any-callee and sequence files are near copies. Never evaluate keccak256 of the full code in the kernel.

notes.incident: This work froze the shared box for about 50 minutes (about 12:58 to 13:48 UTC on 2026-11-11). Cause: a file of my witness stream, Sanity/CodeHash.lean (build TAG witness13), asked the kernel to compute the keccak of the 4,582 code bytes; one Lean process grew to 7.5 GB, used all memory and swap, and was killed by the kernel (exit 137). During that time the box did not answer, and the other agent's own Lean run (lake env lean /home/user/logs/scratch.lean, tokens/uni work) was slowed for about 50 minutes; I did not touch its process. The earlier memory rule (check free memory before a build, 3 threads) did not catch it because the growth came from one process after the build had started. Fix: scripts/wb.sh now has a watchdog that stops any Lean process of its own build above 2600 MB (resident + swap); the file was removed and the fact is kept as an explicit hypothesis. The box was never paused or removed.
